boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Northern Arizona University
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food destinations in Flagstaff with currently published late service hours; confirm day-specific availability before leaving campus.

cards.title: Taco Bell on South Milton
cards.subtitle: 1255 S Milton Rd, Flagstaff
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru when you need a late food stop; check the location page before heading out, since dine-in ends earlier than drive-thru service.
cards.short_summary: A South Milton location with drive-thru service listed until 4 AM every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours of 7 AM–4 AM daily at 1255 S Milton Rd; Sunday dine-in is listed through 11 PM.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 1255 S Milton Rd, Flagstaff
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed 7 AM–4 AM daily; listed dine-in hours end at 11 PM. Check the official page for updates.

cards.title: Wendy’s on South Milton
cards.subtitle: 1601 S Milton Road, Flagstaff
cards.notes: Plan this as a drive-thru or dine-in food option along South Milton; its official page posts the same late closing time for both service modes.
cards.short_summary: A South Milton restaurant listing daily restaurant and drive-thru hours through 1 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s lists restaurant and drive-thru hours of 6:30 AM–1 AM daily for its 1601 S Milton Road location.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant and drive-thru are listed 6:30 AM–1 AM daily; holiday hours may vary.

cards.title: Los Gordos Mexican Food
cards.subtitle: 1051 S Milton Rd, Flagstaff
cards.notes: Choose this South Milton restaurant for a late meal and verify the posted hours on the business site before departure, especially around holidays.
cards.short_summary: A Mexican restaurant at 1051 S Milton Road with midnight hours posted every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Los Gordos Mexican Food lists its Flagstaff location at 1051 S Milton Rd and business hours of 8 AM–12 AM daily.
cards.access_notes: The official site lists 8 AM–12 AM every day; confirm service availability before visiting.

cards.title: Chick-fil-A on South Milton
cards.subtitle: 1000 S Milton Rd, Flagstaff
cards.notes: Use this location for a late-weekday meal when it fits your schedule; the official location page separately confirms dine-in, carry-out, and drive-thru service.
cards.short_summary: A Flagstaff Chick-fil-A location with service modes posted until 11 PM Monday through Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Chick-fil-A lists dine-in, carry-out, and drive-thru hours of 6 AM–11 PM Monday–Saturday at 1000 S Milton Rd; it is closed Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Dine-in, carry-out, and drive-thru are listed until 11 PM Monday–Saturday. Closed Sunday.

cards.title: SoSoBa on Route 66
cards.subtitle: 12 E Route 66, Flagstaff
cards.notes: Head downtown for a food stop with hours posted through midnight; review the restaurant’s current service details before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A Route 66 ramen shop whose official site lists daily hours from 11 AM to midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: SoSoBa lists its Flagstaff address as 12 E Route 66 and hours of 11 AM–midnight every day.
cards.access_notes: Officially listed hours are 11 AM–midnight every day; verify service and seating details before going.

cards.title: Taco Bell on East Butler
cards.subtitle: 1801 E Butler Ave, Flagstaff
cards.notes: For a Butler Avenue late stop, use the drive-thru timing rather than assuming the dining room remains open; the official listing distinguishes the two.
cards.short_summary: An East Butler location with drive-thru hours reaching 2 AM Thursday through Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours through 2 AM Thursday–Saturday and through 1 AM other days at 1801 E Butler Ave.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 1801 E Butler Ave, Flagstaff
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed until 2 AM Thursday–Saturday and 1 AM other days; listed dine-in hours end at 11 PM.

cards.title: Domino’s on East 7th Avenue
cards.subtitle: 2577 E 7th Ave, Flagstaff
cards.notes: Place a carryout or delivery order through the location page and confirm the available time slot before leaving; the page displays the store’s current closing time.
cards.short_summary: An East 7th Avenue Domino’s location showing service until 1 AM on its official store page.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino’s identifies its Flagstaff store at 2577 E 7th Ave and displays that it is open until 1 AM.
cards.access_notes: The official store page displays open until 1 AM; hours can vary, so verify the current order window before going.

cards.title: Teppan Fuji
cards.subtitle: 2500 S Woodlands Village Blvd, Flagstaff
cards.notes: Make this a later dinner option at Woodlands Village and use the restaurant’s posted dinner schedule when planning; Sunday closes earlier than other evenings.
cards.short_summary: A sushi and hibachi restaurant with dinner listed through 10:30 PM Monday through Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Teppan Fuji lists dinner hours of 4:30–10:30 PM Monday–Saturday and 12–9:30 PM Sunday at 2500 S Woodlands Village Blvd.
cards.access_notes: Dinner is listed until 10:30 PM Monday–Saturday and 9:30 PM Sunday; reservations may be useful.

cards.entity_name: Jack in the Box — 3620 E Route 66
cards.title: Jack in the Box on East Route 66
cards.subtitle: 3620 E Route 66, Flagstaff
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru for the latest listed access at this Route 66 location; check the day before you go because weekday and weekend close times differ.
cards.short_summary: An East Route 66 restaurant with drive-thru hours listed until 11 PM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Jack in the Box lists drive-thru hours until 11 PM Friday and Saturday at 3620 E Route 66; other listed days close at 10 PM.
cards.source_title: Jack in the Box — 3620 E Route 66, Flagstaff
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed until 11 PM Friday and Saturday, and 10 PM on other days; lobby closes earlier.

cards.title: Taco Bell on East Route 66
cards.subtitle: 3460 E Route 66, Flagstaff
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru for the late option at this Route 66 location, and review the official page first because the posted dining-room schedule ends earlier.
cards.short_summary: An East Route 66 Taco Bell with drive-thru hours listed through 1 AM every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours of 9 AM–1 AM daily at 3460 E Route 66; listed dine-in hours end at 11 PM.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed 9 AM–1 AM daily; the listed dining-room schedule ends at 11 PM. Confirm before visiting.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named NAU Flagstaff campus places for studying, making, gathering, wellness, culture, and recreation.

cards.title: Cline Library
cards.subtitle: Research, study, collaboration, and creative work
cards.notes: Choose a quiet zone or reserve a study spot, then use the library’s computers, Wi-Fi, printing, and scanning for coursework.
cards.short_summary: A campus library with walk-in and reservable spaces alongside research and technology support.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU says Cline Library offers reserved and walk-in study spaces, technology borrowing, computing, printing, scanning, research support, and creative spaces.
cards.access_notes: Library services and room availability may vary; check the library before visiting.

cards.title: MakerLab
cards.subtitle: Cline Library creative workspace
cards.notes: Bring a project idea and ask about the 3D printers, Glowforge laser cutter, or project consultations during regular library hours.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on Cline Library workspace for turning project ideas into physical creations.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU describes the MakerLab as a creative workspace with 3D printers, a Glowforge laser cutter, and project consultations, open to all skill levels during regular library hours.
cards.source_title: Cline Library learning and study spaces | NAU
cards.access_notes: Located in Cline Library; confirm current library hours and equipment availability before going.

cards.title: Virtual Reality Studio
cards.subtitle: Cline Library immersive creation space
cards.notes: Use one of the studio’s three stations to explore creative or educational VR apps, or plan an immersive project between classes.
cards.short_summary: A three-station VR space inside Cline Library for immersive exploration and creation.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU states that Cline Library’s Virtual Reality Studio has three stations and creative and educational apps for users to explore and create.
cards.source_title: Cline Library learning and study spaces | NAU
cards.access_notes: Cline Library’s floor map lists the Virtual Reality Studio as Room 140; verify access before visiting.

cards.title: One Button Studio
cards.subtitle: Cline Library video-recording studio
cards.notes: Bring a flash drive and record a straightforward video for a class or personal project using the studio’s single-button setup.
cards.short_summary: A user-friendly Cline Library studio designed for recording video without prior production experience.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU says the One Button Studio lets users make high-quality videos with a simple record control and asks visitors to bring a flash drive.
cards.source_title: Cline Library learning and study spaces | NAU
cards.access_notes: Cline Library’s floor map identifies the One Button Studio as Room 139; check availability before arrival.

cards.title: Photography Studio
cards.subtitle: Cline Library portrait and product-photo space
cards.notes: Plan a portrait, product, or still-life session and use the included lighting and equipment for a solo or small-group shoot.
cards.short_summary: A library studio equipped for portraits, product shots, still-life work, and small group sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU says Cline Library’s Photography Studio includes lighting and equipment for portraits, product shots, or still-life images and accommodates groups of up to eight.
cards.source_title: Cline Library learning and study spaces | NAU
cards.access_notes: Cline Library’s floor map lists the Photography Studio as Room 137; confirm current access before visiting.

cards.title: Production Studios
cards.subtitle: Cline Library audio and video creation rooms
cards.notes: Use a production room to record or edit a podcast, voiceover, or video; the library says no prior experience is needed.
cards.short_summary: Dedicated Cline Library rooms for multimedia recording, editing, and content creation.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU describes its Production Studios as spaces for recording, editing, podcasts, video voiceovers, and content creation, with software ready to use.
cards.source_title: Cline Library learning and study spaces | NAU
cards.access_notes: Cline Library’s floor map lists Production Studios 1–3 as Rooms 142–144; verify availability before visiting.

cards.title: University Union
cards.subtitle: Central campus lounge, meeting, dining, and support hub
cards.notes: Use the lounge areas or second floor to meet classmates and study, then locate student support offices in the same building.
cards.short_summary: A central campus building with lounge space, meeting rooms, dining, and student support departments.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU says the University Union has lounge space for student studying and gathering, conference and multipurpose rooms, dining, and student support offices.
cards.source_title: University Union | Unions and Student Activities
cards.access_notes: NAU lists the Union at Building 30, 1050 S. Knoles Drive; individual services and rooms may have separate access rules.

cards.title: Health and Learning Center
cards.subtitle: Second-floor individual and group study areas
cards.notes: Head to the second floor for desks, chairs, couches with side tables, or a private study room when you need a change of setting.
cards.short_summary: A campus building with comfortable second-floor spaces for independent and group study.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU says the Health and Learning Center’s second floor has desks, chairs, couches with side tables, and private study rooms for individual or group work.
cards.source_title: Campus learning and study spaces | NAU
cards.access_notes: Study-room availability may vary; the Recreation Center is inside the Health and Learning Center, Building 25.

cards.title: Native American Cultural Center
cards.subtitle: Campus hub for Native and Indigenous community
cards.notes: Visit respectfully to learn about center programming and connect with its Native and Indigenous student-focused community and support resources.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing NAU cultural center that supports Indigenous students and community connection.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU reports that the Native American Cultural Center has provided a home away from home for NAU’s Indigenous students for more than a decade.
cards.source_title: Culture, care, and community | NAU Stories
cards.access_notes: Respect the center’s programs and any room-use requirements; consult NAU for current visitor and event details.

cards.title: Observatory Field Complex
cards.subtitle: University Drive and San Francisco Street
cards.notes: Check with Campus Recreation about access or reservations, then use the central-campus turf and grass fields for an organized group activity.
cards.short_summary: A central-campus field complex with turf and natural grass areas for recreation and events.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU identifies Observatory Field Complex at University Drive and San Francisco Street, with turf and natural grass fields for open play and pickup games.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation | Have an active lifestyle at NAU
cards.access_notes: Campus Recreation directs users to make reservations; field availability can depend on scheduled activities.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-purchase activities at a free Flagstaff preserve, NAU’s public gallery, and Culture Pass destinations available to eligible NAU students.

cards.title: Walk Don Weaver Trail
cards.subtitle: Picture Canyon Natural & Cultural Preserve · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Bring water, follow the 0.7-mile route to views of the inner canyon, and leave the ruins and petroglyphs exactly as you find them.
cards.short_summary: A short preserve walk with canyon and riparian views.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists Don Weaver as a 0.7-mile trail with inner-canyon, riparian, Pit House ruins, and Petroglyph Overlook views; the preserve is free and open year-round.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public year-round; the City notes some elevation change on this trail.

cards.title: Take the Tom Moody Loop
cards.subtitle: Picture Canyon Natural & Cultural Preserve · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Plan a relaxed 2.8-mile loop, stay on the route, and use the listed Water Bird petroglyph site as a viewing stop—not a touchpoint.
cards.short_summary: A relatively flat loop around the preserve.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes Tom Moody Loop as a 2.8-mile, relatively flat route around the preserve that includes the Water Bird petroglyph site; preserve entry is free.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public year-round. Respect cultural-resource rules and do not climb on or mark petroglyphs.

cards.title: Pause at Petroglyph Overlook
cards.subtitle: Don Weaver Trail · Picture Canyon Natural & Cultural Preserve
cards.notes: Use the overlook to observe from a respectful distance, keep to the trail, and avoid touching, climbing on, or photographing artifacts up close.
cards.short_summary: A designated viewing point reached on Don Weaver Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Petroglyph Overlook as part of Don Weaver Trail and instructs visitors not to deface or remove cultural resources; the preserve is free.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public year-round; cultural-resource etiquette and laws apply.

cards.title: See the Water Bird Petroglyph Site
cards.subtitle: Tom Moody Loop · Picture Canyon Natural & Cultural Preserve
cards.notes: Follow Tom Moody Loop to the named site, look without handling the rock art, and let the visit be a low-impact shared history stop.
cards.short_summary: A named petroglyph viewing stop on the preserve loop.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says Tom Moody Loop includes the main Water Bird petroglyph site and prohibits defacing petroglyphs or removing artifacts; preserve access is free.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public year-round. Do not scratch on boulders, climb on them, or remove artifacts.

cards.title: Photograph Picture Canyon Waterfall
cards.subtitle: Picture Canyon Natural & Cultural Preserve · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Walk in with a camera or phone, frame the waterfall and ponderosa pine from allowed areas, and pack out anything you bring.
cards.short_summary: A year-round-water landmark in the city preserve.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Flagstaff’s only waterfall at Picture Canyon and states that the preserve is free and open to the public year-round.
cards.access_notes: Free year-round public access; do not swim in the Rio de Flag or climb canyon walls.

cards.title: Walk the Arizona Trail Segment
cards.subtitle: Picture Canyon Natural & Cultural Preserve · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Use the easy-to-follow 1.5-mile segment for a walk-and-talk, then return on the marked trail while respecting preserve regulations.
cards.short_summary: A low-elevation-change section of the Arizona Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists a 1.5-mile Arizona Trail segment within Picture Canyon, says it has little elevation change, and states the preserve is free to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public year-round; motorized vehicles are not allowed in the preserve.

cards.title: Browse Beasley Gallery
cards.subtitle: Performing and Fine Arts, Building 37, Room 216 · NAU
cards.notes: Drop in during Wednesday or Thursday public hours to view the rotating exhibitions, then check the gallery’s official channel for updates.
cards.short_summary: NAU’s public gallery for rotating and student exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU states that Beasley Gallery is free and open to the public and gives current Wednesday–Thursday hours of 10 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; listed current hours are Wednesday and Thursday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., or by appointment.

cards.title: Check Out a Lowell Culture Pass
cards.subtitle: Lowell Observatory · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Eligible NAU students can ask at Cline Library’s Ask Us! desk, confirm availability, and use the pass within its seven-day checkout window.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission option for two through Cline Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Cline Library lists Lowell Observatory among available Culture Pass venues; each pass provides one-time free general admission for two people.
cards.access_notes: Culture Pass checkouts are restricted to NAU/CCC students, faculty, and staff; availability is first-come, first-served and special events are excluded.

cards.title: Use a Culture Pass at MNA
cards.subtitle: Museum of Northern Arizona · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Check the pass inventory at Cline Library before making plans, then use the one-time general-admission benefit for a two-person museum outing.
cards.short_summary: Museum entry covered for two by an eligible Culture Pass.
cards.evidence_claim: Cline Library lists the Museum of Northern Arizona as an available Culture Pass venue and says each pass gives free general admission for two people.
cards.access_notes: For NAU/CCC students, faculty, and staff; passes are first-come, first-served and do not cover special events or separately ticketed activities.

cards.title: Reserve a Culture Pass for The Arb
cards.subtitle: The Arb at Flagstaff · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Start at Cline Library’s Ask Us! desk, verify a pass is available, and plan a two-person general-admission visit within seven days.
cards.short_summary: A Flagstaff garden visit covered by a library pass.
cards.evidence_claim: Cline Library lists The Arb at Flagstaff among available Culture Pass destinations and states that each pass is valid for free admission for two people.
cards.access_notes: Culture Pass access is for NAU/CCC students, faculty, and staff; passes are first-come, first-served and exclude special events.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented NAU study environments, from reservable rooms to walk-in seating and technology-supported spaces.

cards.title: Individual Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Cline Library, second and third floors
cards.notes: Reserve an individual room when you need a focused work session; NAU and CCC students may book up to four hours daily, up to two weeks ahead.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms for focused individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: Cline Library lists individual study rooms and states that NAU and CCC students can reserve them for up to four hours per day.
cards.source_title: Learning and Study Spaces | Cline Library
cards.access_notes: NAU and CCC students; reserve up to four hours per day, up to two weeks in advance.

cards.title: Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Cline Library, floors one through three
cards.notes: Book a group room to plan, rehearse, or work through an assignment together; bring collaborators and keep the session within the two-hour daily limit.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms for collaborative coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Cline Library lists group study rooms, including rooms on all three floors, and permits NAU and CCC students to reserve them for two hours per day.
cards.source_title: Learning and Study Spaces | Cline Library
cards.access_notes: NAU and CCC students; reserve up to two hours per day, up to two weeks in advance.

cards.title: Graduate Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Cline Library, third floor
cards.notes: Graduate students can reserve a dedicated room for longer reading or writing blocks; check the scheduler before heading to the third floor.
cards.short_summary: Third-floor reservable rooms for graduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: Cline Library's floor map identifies graduate study rooms 311–326 on the third floor, and its booking policy allows graduate students four hours per day.
cards.source_title: Learning and Study Spaces | Cline Library
cards.access_notes: Graduate students only; reserve up to four hours per day, up to two weeks in advance.

cards.title: Quiet Study Area
cards.subtitle: Cline Library walk-in space
cards.notes: Use this walk-in quiet area for reading, drafting, or problem sets; choose it when you do not need a reservation or a group setup.
cards.short_summary: A walk-in quiet zone in Cline Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Cline Library identifies the Quiet Study Area as one of its walk-in spaces.
cards.source_title: Learning and Study Spaces | Cline Library
cards.access_notes: Walk-in space; confirm building access and current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Open Computers
cards.subtitle: Cline Library walk-in space
cards.notes: Set up at an open computer when your work needs a desktop station; the library lists computer access among its walk-in study options.
cards.short_summary: Walk-in computer access at Cline Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Cline Library lists Open Computers among its walk-in spaces and describes campus computing access with workstations, Wi-Fi, printing, and scanning.
cards.source_title: Learning and Study Spaces | Cline Library
cards.access_notes: Walk-in space; verify availability and current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Open Seating
cards.subtitle: Cline Library walk-in space
cards.notes: Use open seating for a flexible laptop session or a quick reading block; it is a walk-in option, so arrive ready to choose an available seat.
cards.short_summary: Flexible walk-in seating in the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Cline Library identifies Open Seating as a walk-in learning and study space.
cards.source_title: Learning and Study Spaces | Cline Library
cards.access_notes: Walk-in space; confirm building access and current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: The Learning Studio
cards.subtitle: Cline Library Room 249
cards.notes: Use the Learning Studio for technology-supported collaborative work; its writable glass, mobile tables, displays, and videoconferencing tools suit planned group sessions.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, technology-equipped collaboration room.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU says the Learning Studio in Cline Library Room 249 seats 70 and includes writable glass, mobile tables, displays, and videoconferencing tools.
cards.source_title: Cline Library learning and study spaces | NAU
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to library scheduling and access policies; check current availability before planning a session.

cards.title: The MakerLab
cards.subtitle: Cline Library Room 180
cards.notes: Bring a project that benefits from making or prototyping; the MakerLab provides 3D printers, a Glowforge laser cutter, and project consultations during library hours.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on workspace for project-based learning.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU describes the MakerLab as a creative workspace with 3D printers, a Glowforge laser cutter, and project consultations, available during regular library hours.
cards.source_title: Cline Library learning and study spaces | NAU
cards.access_notes: Available during regular library hours; consult staff for equipment use and current availability.

cards.entity_name: Health and Learning Center Second Floor Study Spaces
cards.title: Health and Learning Center Second Floor
cards.subtitle: Health and Learning Center, second floor
cards.notes: Choose a desk, chair, couch with side table, or private study room depending on the task; use the second floor when you need solo or group flexibility.
cards.short_summary: Mixed seating and private rooms in the Health and Learning Center.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU states that the Health and Learning Center's second floor has desks, chairs, couches with side tables, and private study rooms.
cards.source_title: Campus learning and study spaces | NAU
cards.access_notes: Check current building access and private-room availability before visiting.

cards.title: University Union Second Floor
cards.subtitle: University Union, second floor
cards.notes: Settle into the second-floor lounge area for a laptop session or to meet classmates; pair the visit with Academic Student Success Center support if useful.
cards.short_summary: Lounge-style study and gathering space in the Union.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU identifies the University Union, especially its second floor, as a place with lounge areas and space to study and gather; it also houses the Academic Student Success Center.
cards.source_title: Campus learning and study spaces | NAU
cards.access_notes: Check current University Union access and service hours before visiting.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named downtown and Southside stops just beyond Northern Arizona University, each tied to a documented place-specific reason to pause.

cards.title: Start the Walk This Talk route
cards.subtitle: Historic Route 66 corridor — 1 E Route 66
cards.notes: Begin here with a charged phone and earbuds, then follow the self-guided audio route through the Southside Historic District at your own pace.
cards.short_summary: The documented starting point for Flagstaff’s Walk This Talk audio tour.
cards.evidence_claim: The self-guided Walk This Talk route begins on the north side of the Flagstaff Visitor Center at One East Route 66.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor tour route; use the audio-tour instructions and observe crossings near rail traffic.

cards.title: Check the First Friday artwalk listing
cards.subtitle: Aspen Avenue downtown corridor — Heritage Square
cards.notes: Look for the current calendar before heading over; the square’s event program identifies First Friday Artwalk events presented by Flagstaff Arts Council.
cards.short_summary: A downtown square with a documented First Friday arts-program connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Heritage Square Trust’s event information says every first Friday features a First Friday Artwalk event presented by Flagstaff Arts Council.
cards.access_notes: Event dates and programming vary; confirm the current listing before visiting.

cards.title: Look at the current events calendar
cards.subtitle: West Aspen Avenue corridor — 15 W Aspen Ave
cards.notes: Use the theater’s listings to choose a concert or event, then confirm ticketing and entry details directly with the venue before making plans.
cards.short_summary: A named Aspen Avenue venue with a live events listing.
cards.evidence_claim: The Orpheum Theater lists concerts and events and gives its address as 15 West Aspen Avenue in Flagstaff.
cards.access_notes: Events and admission requirements vary; review the specific event listing.

cards.title: Pause under the mature trees
cards.subtitle: West Aspen Avenue corridor — 212 W Aspen Ave
cards.notes: Bring a book or a takeaway snack and use the picnic tables or sitting benches; leave the space ready for the next visitor.
cards.short_summary: A city park with mature trees, picnic tables, and benches.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Flagstaff lists Wheeler Park at 212 W Aspen Avenue with mature trees, picnic tables, and sitting benches.
cards.access_notes: City park hours are sunrise to 10:00 p.m.

cards.title: Plan a library work session
cards.subtitle: West Aspen Avenue corridor — 300 W Aspen Ave
cards.notes: Use the library’s published hours to plan study or browsing time, and note that it sits adjacent to Wheeler Park across from City Hall.
cards.short_summary: A public library beside Wheeler Park with published hours and location.
cards.evidence_claim: The Flagstaff City-Coconino County Public Library is at 300 West Aspen Avenue, adjacent to Wheeler Park, and publishes its hours online.
cards.source_title: Flagstaff City-Coconino County Public Library — Hours & Location
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours and any service notices before traveling.

cards.title: See what the community theater is staging
cards.subtitle: West Cherry Avenue corridor — 11 W Cherry Ave
cards.notes: Review the production calendar and box-office information, then choose a show or educational program that fits your schedule and budget.
cards.short_summary: A community theater with live productions and educational programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Theatrikos states that it offers live musical, comedic, and dramatic productions as well as theatrical youth educational programs; its address is 11 West Cherry Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Performance dates and ticket requirements vary; verify the current calendar and box-office details.

cards.title: Find the Southside Grove sculpture
cards.subtitle: West Phoenix Avenue corridor — between S Milton Rd and S Mikes Pike
cards.notes: Walk through the entry plaza to view the six steel tree-trunk forms and the cultural symbols worked into their surfaces.
cards.short_summary: A transit-hub plaza containing the Southside Grove public artwork.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Southside Grove as a landmark sculpture in the Downtown Connection Center entry plaza on West Phoenix Avenue between South Milton Road and South Mikes Pike.
cards.source_title: City of Flagstaff — Downtown Connection Center
cards.access_notes: The artwork is in a public-transit entry plaza; give riders and transit operations clear space.

cards.title: Read the Route 66 mural from right to left
cards.subtitle: South San Francisco Street corridor — at Phoenix Avenue
cards.notes: Stand back to view the full composition, then use the tour’s interpretation to trace its east-to-west migration story from right to left.
cards.short_summary: A Route 66 mural with a documented viewing direction and interpretation.
cards.evidence_claim: Walk This Talk identifies the Route 66 mural at the northwest corner of San Francisco Street and Phoenix Avenue and directs viewers to read its story from right to left.
cards.access_notes: View from the sidewalk and follow traffic signals when crossing streets.

cards.title: Find the Gandy Dancer sculpture
cards.subtitle: South San Francisco Street corridor — at Historic Route 66
cards.notes: Use the plaza benches for a brief stop and look for the bronze railroad-worker sculpture before continuing the walking route.
cards.short_summary: A small plaza with benches and a documented railroad-worker sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: Walk This Talk describes Santa Fe Plaza at Historic Route 66 and South San Francisco Street as having benches and the bronze Gandy Dancer sculpture by Clyde “Ross” Morgan.
cards.access_notes: The plaza is beside an active rail crossing; cross only at designated signals and remain alert.

cards.title: Use it as a South San Francisco Street landmark
cards.subtitle: North San Francisco Street corridor — 200 N San Francisco St
cards.notes: Orient yourself at this civic landmark before exploring nearby downtown blocks, and keep courthouse business separate from casual sightseeing.
cards.short_summary: A named county civic destination on the downtown San Francisco Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Coconino County states that all court divisions are in the Coconino County Courthouse at 200 North San Francisco Street, Flagstaff.
cards.access_notes: This is an operating courthouse; follow posted security and public-access requirements.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented NAU rituals, symbols, and recurring campus practices centered on Lumberjack spirit and Homecoming.

cards.title: Sprint into the first home game
cards.subtitle: First NAU home football game
cards.notes: If you are a first-year student, join the designated field run just before the football team enters to begin the season.
cards.short_summary: A first-year field sprint launches the football season.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU describes Running of the Freshmen as first-year students sprinting across the field at the first home football game.
cards.access_notes: For first-year students; follow event and stadium staff instructions.

cards.title: Come back for Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Flagstaff campus and downtown parade route
cards.notes: Check the annual schedule, then choose a public Homecoming event such as the parade or football game to take part in campus pride.
cards.short_summary: A week-long NAU reunion tradition dating to 1924.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU states that Homecoming has been a Lumberjack-pride staple since 1924 and is a week-long celebration.
cards.access_notes: Event details vary annually; consult NAU’s current Homecoming schedule.

cards.title: Listen for the touchdown tree cookie
cards.subtitle: NAU football field
cards.notes: At a football game, watch the field after a Lumberjack touchdown for the Logging Sports Club’s ceremonial log slice.
cards.short_summary: A chainsaw-and-log touchdown celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU says a tree-cookie slice is cut on the field to celebrate touchdowns, with the Logging Sports Club involved.
cards.access_notes: Observe from spectator areas and follow stadium instructions.

cards.title: Throw the L-J
cards.subtitle: NAU games, photos, and campus events
cards.notes: Make an L with your right hand and a J with your left when joining a photo or showing Lumberjack pride.
cards.short_summary: NAU’s two-hand L-J school-pride sign.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU identifies the L-J hand sign as part of Lumberjack culture and gives the right-hand L, left-hand J formation.
cards.access_notes: Appropriate for public photos and sporting events.

cards.title: Join the fight-song chorus
cards.subtitle: Game days and Homecoming
cards.notes: Learn the NAU fight song before a game, then sing along with the crowd when the song is played or led.
cards.short_summary: A blue-and-gold rally song for Lumberjack events.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU calls its fight song a rally cry that brings Lumberjacks together on game day and every day.
cards.access_notes: Follow event leaders and stadium guidance.

cards.title: Help spell N-A-U
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week, South Fields
cards.notes: During Welcome Week, wear the provided letters shirt and join the arranged group photo that spells N-A-U from the field.
cards.short_summary: New students form giant NAU letters for a photo.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU lists the NAU Letters Photo as a Welcome Week event where participants spell N-A-U at the South Fields.
cards.source_title: NAU Welcome Week | Discover your community at NAU
cards.access_notes: Scheduled during Welcome Week; verify the current event calendar.

cards.title: Launch your Lumberjack chapter
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week, Walkup Skydome
cards.notes: Attend the Welcome Week celebration in the Skydome to mark your entry into the Lumberjack family with other new students.
cards.short_summary: A Skydome welcome celebration for new Lumberjacks.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU describes Lumberjack Launch as a Skydome celebration of students’ entry into the Lumberjack family.
cards.source_title: NAU Welcome Week | Discover your community at NAU
cards.access_notes: Scheduled during Welcome Week; verify the current event calendar.

cards.title: Spot the Dedicatee tap
cards.subtitle: NAU Homecoming
cards.notes: At Homecoming, watch for the Chain Gang’s ceremonial tap of the selected dedicatee and read the event program for context.
cards.short_summary: Chain Gang members ceremonially tap NAU’s Homecoming dedicatee.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU documents a Chain Gang custom, dating to 1936, of tapping the Homecoming dedicatee.
cards.source_title: The importance of traditions | The NAU Review
cards.access_notes: Observe as part of the official Homecoming program.

cards.title: Watch the Chain Gang’s big chop
cards.subtitle: NAU football game
cards.notes: Look for Chain Gang members and the axe at a football game; the big chop is used to usher in the team.
cards.short_summary: An axe-bearing team entrance ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU reports that Chain Gang members wield the Chain Gang axe for the “big chop” that ushers in the football team.
cards.source_title: The importance of traditions | The NAU Review
cards.access_notes: Observe from spectator areas; only designated participants handle ceremonial equipment.

cards.title: Find the historic logging wheels
cards.subtitle: NAU Homecoming parade, downtown Flagstaff
cards.notes: Choose a safe public viewing spot along the parade route and look for the historic logging wheels in the Homecoming procession.
cards.short_summary: Historic logging wheels anchor NAU’s annual parade.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU identifies the historic logging wheels as the centerpiece of the annual Homecoming parade since 1932.
cards.source_title: The importance of traditions | The NAU Review
cards.access_notes: Use public parade viewing areas and follow local event controls.
